He said, "I have believed in your Lord, so listen to me."
On entering Paradise he wished his people knew how Allah had forgiven him.
hard.explain: Surah Ya-Sin tells of a man who came running from the far end of the city urging his people to follow the messengers. When told to enter Paradise, he wished his people knew.

clues: He is mentioned in Surah Ghafir.
He hid his faith.
He spoke up when Fir'awn wanted to kill Musa.
He asked, "Will you kill a man because he says my Lord is Allah?"
He was from the family of Fir'awn himself.
hard.explain: Surah Ghafir tells of a believing man of Fir'awn's family, who had hidden his faith, defending Musa.

clues: Their story is in Surah Al-Ma'idah.
Each offered a sacrifice.
Only one was accepted.
One killed the other.
A raven showed the killer how to bury his brother.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Ma'idah tells the story of the two sons of Adam. Allah sent a raven to show the killer how to hide his brother's body.

clues: Their story is in Surah Al-Qalam.
They swore to harvest their fruit early in the morning.
They did not say "in sha' Allah".
They meant to keep the poor away.
They found their garden burned and black.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Qalam tells of the owners of a garden who planned to harvest it without giving the poor, and found it destroyed overnight.

clues: His story is in Surah Al-Kahf.
He had two gardens with a river between them.
He told his friend, "I have more wealth than you."
He thought his garden would never perish.
He ended up wringing his hands over what he had spent on it.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Kahf gives the parable of two men, one given two gardens. He boasted, and his fruit was destroyed.

hard.answer: The man who died for a hundred years
options: The man who died for a hundred years
clues: His story is in Surah Al-Baqarah.
He passed by a town in ruins.
He asked how Allah could bring it back to life.
Allah caused him to die and then raised him.
His food had not spoiled, but his donkey had turned to bones.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Baqarah tells of the man who passed a ruined town. Allah made him die for a hundred years and then raised him, as a sign.

clues: It was a gift to a prophet.
It blew at his command.
Its morning journey was a month's travel.
Its evening journey was a month's travel too.
It was made subject to Sulayman.
hard.explain: Allah says, "And to Sulayman the wind; its morning course was a month and its evening course a month."

hard.answer: The coats of mail of Dawud
options: The coats of mail of Dawud
clues: It was a skill given to a prophet.
Iron was made soft for him.
Allah told him to measure the links well.
It protected people in battle.
He was taught how to make armour.
hard.explain: Allah made iron soft for Dawud and taught him to make coats of mail to protect people in battle.

clues: It is a term of hadith science.
It describes how many narrated something.
Most hadith fall into it.
It does not reach the level of tawatur.
It can still be sahih.
hard.explain: An ahad hadith is any narration that does not reach the level of mutawatir. Many of them are authentic.

clues: It is a grade of hadith.
It falls below hasan.
It lacks one or more conditions of acceptance.
It can be caused by a broken chain or a weak narrator.
It means weak.
hard.explain: A da'if hadith fails to meet the conditions of a sahih or hasan hadith, such as a connected chain or reliable narrators.

clues: It is a grade of hadith.
It is accepted as evidence.
It sits between sahih and da'if.
Its narrators are reliable but some are less precise.
Al-Tirmidhi used it very often.
hard.explain: A hasan hadith has a connected chain of trustworthy narrators whose precision is slightly below that of a sahih hadith.

clues: It is a grade of hadith.
It is the highest grade of acceptance.
Its chain is connected throughout.
Its narrators are upright and precise, with no hidden defect.
It means authentic or sound.
hard.explain: A sahih hadith has a connected chain of upright, precise narrators and is free of irregularity and hidden defects.

clues: It is one category of tawhid as scholars explain it.
It concerns Allah's actions.
It means He alone creates, provides and controls all things.
Even the idol worshippers of Makkah affirmed it.
It is the oneness of Lordship.
hard.explain: Al-Fatihah opens with "Lord of the worlds". The Qur'an notes that the pagans admitted Allah created the heavens and earth.

clues: It is one category of tawhid as scholars explain it.
It concerns the actions of the servants.
Every messenger called his people to it.
It means all worship is for Allah alone.
"You alone we worship" expresses it.
hard.explain: Every messenger said, "Worship Allah, you have no god but Him." Al-Fatihah says, "You alone we worship."

clues: It is one category of tawhid as scholars explain it.
It concerns how Allah is described.
It affirms what Allah affirmed for Himself.
It rejects likening Him to His creation.
"There is nothing like Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing" sums it up.
hard.explain: Surah Ash-Shura says, "There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Hearer, the Seer."

clues: It was fought in the time of Umar.
It was fought in Persia.
The Muslim commander al-Nu'man ibn Muqarrin was martyred in it.
It broke the power of the Sasanian army.
It is called "the victory of victories".
hard.explain: Nahawand, around 21 AH, ended organised Sasanian resistance and became known as the victory of victories.

clues: It was fought against the Crusaders.
It was fought near Lake Tiberias.
The Crusader army suffered terribly from thirst.
It happened in 583 AH.
Salah al-Din's victory there opened the way to Jerusalem.
hard.explain: At Hattin in 583 AH Salah al-Din destroyed the Crusader army, and Jerusalem was retaken a few months later.

clues: It was fought in Palestine.
It came two years after the fall of Baghdad.
It was fought against the Mongols.
The Mamluks of Egypt won it.
Qutuz and Baybars led the Muslims there in 658 AH.
hard.explain: At Ain Jalut in 658 AH the Mamluks under Qutuz, with Baybars, defeated the Mongols and halted their advance.

clues: Muslims tried to take this city for centuries.
Abu Ayyub al-Ansari is buried near its walls.
Ships were carried overland to reach its harbour.
It was taken by Sultan Mehmed II.
It happened in 857 AH and the city became Istanbul.
hard.explain: Sultan Mehmed II took Constantinople in 857 AH (1453 CE), after centuries of attempts going back to the Umayyads.

clues: It was a trial imposed by the state.
It began under the Abbasid caliph al-Ma'mun.
Scholars were questioned about the nature of the Qur'an.
Ahmad ibn Hanbal refused to say the Qur'an was created.
Its name means "the trial" or "the inquisition".
hard.explain: In the Mihnah, scholars were forced to declare the Qur'an created. Ahmad ibn Hanbal refused and was imprisoned and flogged.

clues: It was fought between Muslims.
It was fought on the Euphrates in 37 AH.
Ammar ibn Yasir was killed in it.
Copies of the Qur'an were raised on spears.
It ended in an arbitration.
hard.explain: At Siffin in 37 AH Ammar ibn Yasir was killed. The fighting ended when arbitration was agreed.

clues: It is a place in Iraq.
It is near the Euphrates.
A tragedy happened there on the 10th of Muharram.
It happened in 61 AH.
Al-Husayn ibn Ali was martyred there.
hard.explain: Al-Husayn ibn Ali, the Prophet's grandson, was martyred at Karbala on the 10th of Muharram, 61 AH.

clues: It was a year of hardship.
It happened in the time of Umar.
Drought and famine struck the Hijaz.
Umar refused to eat better than his people until it ended.
Its name means "the year of ashes".
hard.explain: In 18 AH a severe drought and famine struck Arabia. Umar shared the hardship, and historians relate he asked for rain through al-Abbas.

clues: It struck al-Sham in the time of Umar.
Umar turned back from the journey there.
He was told the Prophet ﷺ said not to enter a land with plague.
Abu Ubaydah and Mu'adh ibn Jabal died in it.
It is named after a village in Palestine.
hard.explain: Umar turned back at Sargh on hearing of the plague in al-Sham, after Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf told him the Prophet's instruction. Abu Ubaydah and Mu'adh died in the plague of Amwas.

clues: It is a month.
It is the third month of the Islamic year.
The Prophet ﷺ arrived in Madinah in it.
Most historians date his birth to it.
He passed away in it in 11 AH.
hard.explain: Rabi' al-Awwal is the month of the Prophet's arrival in Madinah and of his passing in 11 AH, and most date his birth to it.

clues: It is a month.
It is the second month of the Islamic year.
Pre-Islamic Arabs considered it unlucky.
The Prophet ﷺ rejected that belief.
He said, "There is no Safar."
hard.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said there is no contagion without Allah's decree, no evil omen, no hamah and no Safar, rejecting the belief that it was an unlucky month.

clues: It is a month.
It is one of the four sacred months.
It is the eleventh month of the Islamic year.
The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was made in it.
It comes just before the month of Hajj.
hard.explain: Dhul-Qa'dah is the first of the three consecutive sacred months. Several of the Prophet's umrahs, including Hudaybiyyah, took place in it.

clues: It is made of cloth.
It is used only once.
It is sunnah for it to be white.
The Prophet ﷺ was wrapped in three white sheets.
It is the shroud.
hard.explain: Aishah said the Prophet ﷺ was shrouded in three white Yemeni sheets, with no shirt or turban among them.

clues: It is a way of performing Hajj.
Umrah is done first in the months of Hajj.
The pilgrim leaves ihram between the two.
An offering, or a fast, is required.
The Prophet ﷺ told those without a sacrificial animal to do it at the Farewell Pilgrimage.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Baqarah says whoever combines Umrah with Hajj must make an offering, or fast if unable.

clues: It is a rite of Hajj and Umrah.
It marks leaving ihram.
The Prophet ﷺ prayed three times for those who do it.
It is better than just trimming.
It is shaving the head.
hard.explain: The Prophet ﷺ prayed for mercy on those who shave their heads, three times, before including those who trim.

clues: It is made of cloth.
It is black, with gold embroidery.
It is replaced every year.
Its embroidered band carries verses of the Qur'an.
It is the covering of the Ka'bah.
hard.explain: The kiswah is the cloth that covers the Ka'bah, renewed every year.

statements: The Qur'an has 114 surahs.
Surah Al-Fatihah has seven ayahs.
The Qur'an was revealed to Prophet Musa.
easy.explain: The Qur'an was revealed to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. Musa received the Tawrat. The other two statements are correct.

statements: There are five obligatory prayers each day.
Ramadan is the ninth month of the Islamic calendar.
Hajj is performed in the month of Rajab.
easy.explain: Hajj is performed in Dhul-Hijjah, the twelfth month. Umrah may be performed at any time of year, which is sometimes the source of the confusion.

statements: The Ka'bah is in Makkah.
Muslims face the Ka'bah during prayer.
The Ka'bah was built by Prophet Musa.
easy.explain: The Qur'an describes Ibrahim and his son Isma'il raising the foundations of the Ka'bah. Musa is not connected with its construction.

statements: Zakat is one of the five pillars of Islam.
Fasting the month of Ramadan is obligatory.
There are seven pillars of Islam.
easy.explain: There are five pillars: the shahada, salah, zakat, fasting Ramadan, and Hajj for those able.

statements: The first revelation came while the Prophet ﷺ was at the cave of Hira.
The Prophet ﷺ migrated from Makkah to Madinah.
The Prophet ﷺ passed away in Makkah.
easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ passed away in Madinah, in 11 AH, and is buried there.

statements: Surah Al-Fatihah is recited in every unit of prayer.
The Qur'an was revealed in Arabic.
The Qur'an was revealed all at once in a single night.
easy.explain: The Qur'an was revealed in stages over approximately 23 years. What is described as happening in a single blessed night is the beginning of its revelation.

statements: Muslims fast during the month of Ramadan.
The fast begins at dawn and ends at sunset.
The fast begins at sunset and ends at dawn.
easy.explain: The fast runs from the break of dawn until sunset. Eating is permitted during the night.

statements: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was born in Makkah.
The Qur'an was revealed in Arabic.
The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ could not be described as a messenger.
easy.explain: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is a messenger of Allah; affirming this is part of the shahada itself.

statements: There are 114 surahs in the Qur'an.
Surah Al-Baqarah is the longest surah.
Surah Al-Baqarah is the first surah in the mushaf.
easy.explain: Al-Fatihah is the first surah. Al-Baqarah is the second, and the longest at 286 ayahs.

statements: Eid al-Fitr comes at the end of Ramadan.
Eid al-Adha comes during the month of Hajj.
Eid al-Adha comes at the end of Ramadan.
easy.explain: Eid al-Fitr ends Ramadan, on 1 Shawwal. Eid al-Adha falls on 10 Dhul-Hijjah, during the days of Hajj.

statements: Muslims pray facing the Ka'bah.
The Ka'bah is in Makkah.
Muslims pray facing Madinah.
easy.explain: The qiblah is the Ka'bah in Makkah, not Madinah. Madinah holds the Prophet's mosque but is not the direction of prayer.

statements: Zakat is given to those in need.
Zakat is one of the five pillars.
Zakat is a voluntary charity with no fixed rules.
easy.explain: Zakat is obligatory, with a defined threshold (nisab), rate and set of eligible recipients. The voluntary charity is sadaqah.

statements: Jumu'ah prayer is held on Friday.
Jumu'ah is preceded by a sermon.
Jumu'ah prayer is held on Saturday.
easy.explain: Jumu'ah is the Friday congregational prayer, and it is preceded by the khutbah.

statements: Wudu is performed before prayer.
Wudu involves washing the face, arms and feet.
Wudu is performed only once a year.
easy.explain: Wudu is performed whenever it has been invalidated and prayer is to be offered — potentially several times a day.

statements: The Qur'an was revealed to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
The Tawrat was given to Prophet Musa.
The Zabur was given to Prophet Isa.
easy.explain: The Zabur was given to Prophet Dawud. Prophet Isa was given the Injil.

statements: Hajj is performed in Dhul-Hijjah.
Umrah can be performed at any time of year.
Hajj can be performed at any time of year.
easy.explain: Hajj has a fixed season in Dhul-Hijjah. It is Umrah that may be performed at any time.

statements: Fajr is prayed before sunrise.
Maghrib is prayed after sunset.
Isha is prayed before Maghrib.
easy.explain: Isha comes after Maghrib. The order through the day is Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha.

statements: The Ka'bah is a cube-shaped structure.
Pilgrims walk around the Ka'bah seven times.
Pilgrims walk around the Ka'bah three times.
easy.explain: Tawaf consists of seven circuits around the Ka'bah.

statements: Angels are created beings.
Jibril brought revelation to the prophets.
Jibril was a prophet sent to his own people.
easy.explain: Jibril is an angel, not a prophet. Prophets are human beings chosen from among their own people.

statements: Surah Al-Fatihah is recited in every rak'ah.
Surah Al-Fatihah has seven ayahs.
Surah Al-Fatihah is the last surah in the Qur'an.
easy.explain: Al-Fatihah is the first surah. The last is An-Nas, surah 114.

statements: The shahada has two parts.
Saying the shahada sincerely is how one enters Islam.
The shahada is one of the pillars of iman.
easy.explain: The shahada is the first of the five pillars of Islam. The articles of iman are a separate list of six beliefs.

statements: Prophet Nuh built an ark.
Prophet Musa was given the Tawrat.
Prophet Nuh was given the Tawrat.
easy.explain: The Tawrat was given to Musa. No scripture is named in the Qur'an as having been given to Nuh.

statements: Maryam is the mother of Prophet Isa.
Maryam is named in the Qur'an.
Maryam was a prophet.
easy.explain: Maryam is honoured as chosen above the women of the worlds, and a surah bears her name, but she is not counted among the prophets.

statements: Muslims greet one another with as-salamu alaykum.
The greeting means peace be upon you.
The greeting is only used once a year.
easy.explain: The greeting of peace is used in everyday life, whenever Muslims meet.

statements: Fasting is obligatory during Ramadan.
Children before puberty are not obliged to fast.
Everyone without exception must fast, including the seriously ill.
easy.explain: The Qur'an exempts the sick and the traveller, who make up the days later; those permanently unable to fast give fidyah instead.

statements: The Qur'an has 114 surahs.
Surah An-Nas is the last surah.
Surah An-Nas is the first surah.
easy.explain: An-Nas is surah 114, the last. Al-Fatihah is the first.

statements: Hajj takes place in Makkah.
Tawaf is performed around the Ka'bah.
Tawaf is performed around Mount Arafah.
easy.explain: Tawaf is the circling of the Ka'bah. Arafah is a plain where pilgrims stand on the 9th of Dhul-Hijjah; there is no circling there.

statements: Angels are created from light, according to hadith.
Angels do not disobey Allah.
Angels are a kind of prophet.
easy.explain: Angels and prophets are entirely distinct. Prophets are human beings chosen from among people.

statements: Muslims believe in all the prophets.
Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is the final prophet.
Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is the first prophet.
easy.explain: Adam, ʿalayhi al-salām, is the first. Muhammad ﷺ is the final prophet, the seal of the prophets.

statements: Salah is performed five times a day.
Each salah has a set number of rak'ahs.
Each of the five prayers has the same number of rak'ahs.
easy.explain: Fajr has two rak'ahs, Maghrib three, and Dhuhr, Asr and Isha four each.

statements: The Qur'an is the word of Allah.
It was revealed through the angel Jibril.
It was written by the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ himself.
easy.explain: The Qur'an is revelation, not authorship. It was conveyed through Jibril, memorised and recorded by scribes among the companions.

statements: A mosque is a place of worship.
The imam leads the congregational prayer.
The imam must be an angel.
easy.explain: The imam is a person who leads the prayer; any qualified Muslim man may do so.

statements: Zakat helps those in need.
Sadaqah is voluntary.
Sadaqah is obligatory and zakat is voluntary.
easy.explain: It is the other way round: zakat is obligatory with fixed rules, while sadaqah is voluntary.

statements: Laylat al-Qadr falls in Ramadan.
Eid al-Fitr falls in Shawwal.
Laylat al-Qadr falls in Shawwal.
easy.explain: Laylat al-Qadr is sought in the last ten nights of Ramadan. Shawwal is the month that follows, beginning with Eid al-Fitr.

statements: Prophet Ibrahim is associated with the Ka'bah.
Prophet Isma'il was his son.
Prophet Musa was his son.
easy.explain: Isma'il and Ishaq were sons of Ibrahim. Musa came many generations later.

statements: The adhan is the call to prayer.
It is called before each obligatory prayer.
It is called only on Fridays.
easy.explain: The adhan precedes each of the five daily prayers, every day.

statements: Muslims fast from food and drink while fasting.
The fast is broken at sunset.
The fast is broken at midnight.
easy.explain: The fast ends at sunset with iftar, at the time of the Maghrib prayer.

statements: Surah Al-Fatihah opens the Qur'an.
It is recited in every rak'ah.
It has seventy ayahs.
easy.explain: Surah Al-Fatihah has seven ayahs, not seventy.

statements: Jibril brought the first revelation.
The first revelation came at the cave of Hira.
The first revelation came in Madinah.
easy.explain: The first revelation came at the cave of Hira, near Makkah, years before the migration to Madinah.

statements: Wudu can be invalidated and then repeated.
Ghusl is a full bath required in certain states.
Ghusl and wudu are exactly the same thing.
easy.explain: Wudu is the partial ablution before prayer; ghusl is the complete washing of the body required in specific states of impurity.

statements: Believing in the angels is an article of faith.
Believing in the Last Day is an article of faith.
Believing in the five pillars is one of the six articles of faith.
easy.explain: The five pillars are acts of Islam, not items in the list of six beliefs. The six articles are Allah, angels, books, messengers, the Last Day, and divine decree.

statements: Prophet Sulayman was a king as well as a prophet.
Prophet Dawud was given the Zabur.
Prophet Sulayman was given the Zabur.
easy.explain: The Zabur was given to Dawud, the father of Sulayman.

statements: Prophet Yunus was swallowed by a great fish.
Prophet Ayyub is known for his patience.
Prophet Ayyub was swallowed by a great fish.
easy.explain: That was Yunus. Ayyub is remembered for patience through severe illness and loss.

statements: Adam was the first human being.
Muhammad ﷺ is the final prophet.
Adam was the final prophet.
easy.explain: Adam, ʿalayhi al-salām, was the first. Muhammad ﷺ is the seal of the prophets.

statements: The Qur'an is divided into 30 ajza.
Many people read one juz a night in Ramadan.
The Qur'an is divided into 30 surahs.
easy.explain: The Qur'an has 114 surahs. It is the juz divisions that number thirty.

statements: Jannah is the reward of the believers.
Jahannam is a place of punishment.
Jannah is a place of punishment.
easy.explain: Jannah is paradise; Jahannam is the Fire.

statements: Iblis refused to prostrate to Adam.
Iblis was of the jinn.
Iblis was one of the angels.
easy.explain: The Qur'an states explicitly that Iblis was of the jinn. Angels do not disobey what they are commanded.

statements: SubhanAllah is a phrase of remembrance.
Alhamdulillah means all praise is for Allah.
Alhamdulillah means Allah is the Greatest.
easy.explain: Allahu akbar means Allah is the Greatest. Alhamdulillah is praise.

statements: A hafiz has memorised the whole Qur'an.
The imam leads the prayer.
A hafiz is someone who leads the prayer.
easy.explain: A hafiz is a memoriser of the Qur'an. Leading the prayer is the role of the imam, though a hafiz often does so.

statements: Halal means permitted.
Haram means forbidden.
Halal means forbidden.
easy.explain: Halal is the permitted and haram the forbidden — the two are opposites.

statements: Prophet Harun was the brother of Musa.
Prophet Isma'il was a son of Ibrahim.
Prophet Harun was a son of Ibrahim.
easy.explain: Harun was the brother of Musa, many generations after Ibrahim.

statements: The mihrab shows the direction of prayer.
The minbar is used for the sermon.
The minbar shows the direction of prayer.
easy.explain: The mihrab is the niche marking the qiblah; the minbar is the pulpit.

statements: Zakat al-Fitr is given before the Eid prayer.
Zakat al-Mal is calculated on wealth.
Zakat al-Fitr is calculated on wealth.
easy.explain: Zakat al-Fitr is a fixed amount per person. Zakat al-Mal is the one calculated against wealth and the nisab.

statements: Tayammum uses clean earth.
Tayammum is used when water is unavailable.
Tayammum is performed with water.
easy.explain: Tayammum is specifically the dry alternative to wudu, used when water is unavailable or harmful.

statements: Prophet Isa was given the Injil.
Prophet Musa was given the Tawrat.
Prophet Isa was given the Tawrat.
easy.explain: The Tawrat was given to Musa and the Injil to Isa, ʿalayhim al-salām.

statements: Qiyam is the standing position in prayer.
Sujud is prostration.
Qiyam is prostration.
easy.explain: Qiyam is standing; sujud is prostration.

statements: Prophet Nuh's people were destroyed by a flood.
Prophet Nuh built an ark.
Prophet Nuh's people were destroyed by an earthquake.
easy.explain: The punishment of Nuh's people was the flood, from which those with him in the ark were saved.

statements: Istighfar is seeking forgiveness.
Takbir is saying Allahu akbar.
Istighfar is saying Allahu akbar.
easy.explain: Istighfar is seeking forgiveness, commonly Astaghfirullah. Takbir is Allahu akbar.

statements: Surah Al-Kawthar is the shortest surah.
Surah Al-Baqarah is the longest.
Surah Al-Kawthar is the longest surah.
easy.explain: Al-Kawthar has three ayahs; Al-Baqarah has 286.

statements: Prophet Yusuf was thrown into a well by his brothers.
A surah is named after Yusuf.
Prophet Yusuf was thrown into a well by his father.
easy.explain: It was his brothers. His father Ya'qub grieved his loss for many years.

statements: Maryam is the mother of Isa.
Surah Maryam is named after her.
Maryam is the mother of Musa.
easy.explain: Maryam is the mother of Isa, ʿalayhi al-salām.

statements: Surah Al-Balad has 20 ayat.
Surah An-Nisa was revealed in Makkah.
Surah Al-Ikhlas has 4 ayat.
easy.explain: Surah An-Nisa is a Madani surah, revealed in Madinah. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: Surah Al-Humazah was revealed in Makkah.
Surah 'Abasa has 32 ayat.
The name Surah Al-Qadr means “The Power”.
easy.explain: Surah 'Abasa has 42 ayat, not 32. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: Surah Al-Waqi'ah comes right after Surah At-Tur.
Surah Al-Fil comes right after Surah Al-Humazah.
Surah Ya-Sin was revealed in Makkah.
easy.explain: Surah Al-Waqi'ah comes right after Surah Ar-Rahman, not Surah At-Tur. The other two statements are correct.

statements: The name Surah An-Nas means “Mankind”.
The name Surah Al-Bayyinah means “The Clear Proof”.
Surah Al-Qari'ah was revealed in Madinah.
easy.explain: Surah Al-Qari'ah is a Makki surah, revealed in Makkah. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Surah Al-Kafirun was revealed in Makkah.
Surah Al-Balad has 12 ayat.
The name Surah Al-Ghashiyah means “The Overwhelming”.
easy.explain: Surah Al-Balad has 20 ayat, not 12. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: Surah Quraysh comes right after Surah Al-Fil.
Surah Az-Zalzalah has 12 ayat.
The name Surah Al-Ghashiyah means “The Overwhelming”.
easy.explain: Surah Az-Zalzalah has 8 ayat, not 12. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: Surah At-Tariq comes right after Surah Al-Balad.
Surah Al-Layl comes right after Surah Ash-Shams.
Surah Al-Waqi'ah has 96 ayat.
easy.explain: Surah At-Tariq comes right after Surah Al-Buruj, not Surah Al-Balad. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

Witr is prayed before Fajr's adhan only on Fridays.
medium.explain: Witr is prayed between Isha and Fajr. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Every child is born on the fitrah.
The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was made with Quraysh.
The Prophet ﷺ said the best of you are those who own the most land.
medium.explain: He said, "The best of you are those who learn the Qur'an and teach it." The other two statements are correct.

statements: Al-Fatihah is recited in every rak'ah of the prayer.
Mu'adh ibn Jabal was sent to Persia.
Surah Al-Fath was revealed after Hudaybiyyah.
medium.explain: The Prophet ﷺ sent Mu'adh to Yemen. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Surah Al-Ikhlas is equal to a third of the Qur'an.
Haman was the brother of Musa.
I'tikaf is usually done in the last ten days of Ramadan.
medium.explain: Haman served Fir'awn. Musa's brother was Harun. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Surah Al-Hujurat teaches not to mock other people.
The Prophet ﷺ said the most beloved deeds to Allah are the most consistent, even if small.
The Prophet ﷺ said the world is a paradise for the believer.
medium.explain: The world is the believer's prison and the disbeliever's paradise. The other two statements are correct.

statements: The Battle of Badr was the first major battle of Islam.
The Prophet ﷺ said a surah of thirty verses, Al-Mulk, intercedes for the one who recites it.
Allah says with ease comes only hardship.
medium.explain: Surah Ash-Sharh: with hardship comes ease, twice. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Ayat al-Kursi is the greatest verse in the Qur'an.
Surah Al-Ma'un praises those who pray only to be seen.
The People of the Cave slept for 309 years.
medium.explain: It warns "those who want to be seen". The other two statements are correct.

statements: The Prophet ﷺ prayed at night until his feet swelled.
Ibrahim's father was named Azar in the Qur'an.
Allah says people must be forced into religion.
medium.explain: Al-Baqarah 256: there is no compulsion in religion. The other two statements are correct.

statements: The Ansar were the Muslims of Madinah.
Tahajjud is prayed at noon.
Yahya was the son of Zakariyya.
medium.explain: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ, "And in some part of the night, pray tahajjud." The other two statements are correct.

statements: The Prophet ﷺ encouraged cutting ties with relatives.
The miqat for the people of Madinah is Dhul-Hulayfah.
Malik is the keeper of Hell.
medium.explain: He said the one who cuts ties of kinship will not enter Paradise. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Zamzam appeared for Hajar and her son.
Salih was sent to Thamud.
Shu'ayb was sent to 'Ad.
medium.explain: Shu'ayb was sent to Madyan. Hud was sent to 'Ad. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Allah burdens every soul beyond what it can bear.
The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was made with Quraysh.
The Farewell Pilgrimage was in 10 AH.
medium.explain: The end of Al-Baqarah says Allah tasks no soul beyond its capacity. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Mu'awiyah sent standard copies of the Qur'an to the main cities.
The miqat for the people of Madinah is Dhul-Hulayfah.
Isma'il helped his father build the Ka'bah.
medium.explain: Uthman had copies made from Hafsah's sheets and sent them out. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Ayyub is known for building the Ka'bah.
The Prophet ﷺ said none of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
Abu Lahab is the only opponent of the Prophet named in the Qur'an.
medium.explain: Allah says of Ayyub, "We found him patient." The other two statements are correct.

statements: The Qur'an forbids wine and gambling.
The Prophet ﷺ said the world is a prison for the believer.
Hajar ran between Arafah and Mina seven times.
medium.explain: Hajar ran between Safa and Marwah looking for water, and pilgrims do the same. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Zakat has three categories of recipients.
The Qur'an was first gathered into one volume under Abu Bakr.
Pork is forbidden in the Qur'an.
medium.explain: Surah At-Tawbah lists eight categories. The other two statements are correct.

statements: The Prophet ﷺ said the best of you are those who learn the Qur'an and teach it.
Allah says with hardship comes ease.
The Muslims at Badr numbered about three thousand.
medium.explain: Al-Bara' said the people of Badr were about the number of Talut's men, a little over three hundred. The other two statements are correct.

statements: The Muhajirun were the Muslims who migrated from Makkah.
Khalid was called the trustworthy one of this ummah.
Abu Bakr accompanied the Prophet ﷺ on the Hijrah.
medium.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said the trustworthy one of this ummah is Abu Ubaydah. The other two statements are correct.

statements: The Prophet ﷺ said the Fire is surrounded by hardships.
Zayd ibn Harithah is the only companion named in the Qur'an.
The Muslims first faced Jerusalem in prayer.
medium.explain: Paradise is surrounded by hardships, and the Fire by desires. The other two statements are correct.

statements: The Prophet ﷺ prayed at night until his feet swelled.
Lut's people lived in the time of Ibrahim.
The Prophet ﷺ said the most beloved deeds to Allah are the biggest, even if rare.
medium.explain: The most beloved deed to Allah is the most regular, even if little. The other two statements are correct.

statements: I'tikaf is only allowed in the first ten days of Ramadan.
The last two verses of Al-Baqarah suffice the one who recites them at night.
The Ansar were the Muslims of Madinah.
medium.explain: The Prophet ﷺ used to make i'tikaf in the last ten days of Ramadan. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Allah says in Surah Al-Baqarah that He is far and does not answer.
The People of the Cave slept for 309 years.
Surah Al-Ikhlas is equal to a third of the Qur'an.
medium.explain: When My servants ask you about Me, I am near. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Allah says there is no compulsion in religion.
A trench was dug around Madinah in the Battle of the Confederates.
Ruku' is the position in which a servant is closest to his Lord.
medium.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said the closest a servant is to his Lord is when he is prostrating. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Pilgrims spend the night at Muzdalifah after Arafah.
Witr is prayed after Isha.
Anas ibn Malik served the Prophet ﷺ for two years.
medium.explain: Anas said he served the Prophet ﷺ for ten years. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Surah Al-Kahf is recommended on Mondays.
Travellers may shorten four-rak'ah prayers to two.
Shu'ayb was sent to Madyan.
medium.explain: Reciting Al-Kahf on Friday is narrated to bring light between the two Fridays. The other two statements are correct.

statements: The Qur'an calls the believers brothers.
Surah Al-Fath was revealed after Hudaybiyyah.
Surah Al-Qadr says the jinn descend on Laylat al-Qadr.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Qadr: the angels and the Spirit descend in it by the permission of their Lord. The other two statements are correct.

statements: There are fifteen places of prostration in the Qur'an in the common count.
The Prophet ﷺ forbade cutting ties of kinship.
Ridwan is named in the Qur'an as the keeper of Hell.
medium.explain: The Qur'an names Malik as the keeper of the Fire. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Musa met al-Khidr where the two seas meet.
Al-Khidr damaged a boat to save it from a king.
Surah Al-Asr says mankind is always successful.
medium.explain: Al-Asr: man is in loss, except those who believe, do righteous deeds and counsel truth and patience. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Al-Fatihah is recited in every rak'ah of the prayer.
Salih was sent to Madyan.
Surah Al-Ma'un warns those who pray only to be seen.
medium.explain: Salih was sent to Thamud. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Fasting the day of Arafah expiates two years of sins.
Mu'adh ibn Jabal was sent to Yemen.
Abu Bakr was called the Sword of Allah.
medium.explain: The Prophet ﷺ called Khalid a sword from the swords of Allah. The other two statements are correct.

statements: The Farewell Pilgrimage was in 10 AH.
Haman was the minister of Fir'awn.
The Prophet ﷺ travelled to Damascus to invite its people.
medium.explain: He went to Ta'if, and its people rejected him. The other two statements are correct.

statements: The qiblah was changed in the tenth year after the Hijrah.
Ya'juj and Ma'juj were held back by a barrier.
Allah says the most honoured of you is the most righteous.
medium.explain: The qiblah changed about sixteen or seventeen months after the Hijrah. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Fasting Ashura expiates the previous year.
The Battle of Badr was the first major battle of Islam.
Harut and Marut were sent down in Makkah.
medium.explain: Al-Baqarah places them in Babylon. The other two statements are correct.

statements: The Prophet ﷺ said the strongest believer is more beloved to Allah than the weak one, and in both there is good.
Surah Al-Hujurat teaches not to mock other people.
Ali married two daughters of the Prophet ﷺ.
medium.explain: Uthman married Ruqayyah and then Umm Kulthum. Ali married Fatimah. The other two statements are correct.

statements: The Expedition of Tabuk was against the Persians.
Yunus is called Dhun-Nun in the Qur'an.
Sulayman had jinn working for him.
medium.explain: Tabuk, in 9 AH, was a march north to face the Byzantines. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Hud was sent to the people of 'Ad.
The best prayer after the obligatory ones is the Duha prayer.
Zayd ibn Thabit led the gathering of the Qur'an.
medium.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said the best prayer after the obligatory ones is the prayer at night. The other two statements are correct.

statements: The Prophet ﷺ said Surah Al-Kawthar intercedes for the one who recites it until he is forgiven.
Every child is born on the fitrah.
The Dajjal is blind in one eye.
medium.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said a surah of thirty verses interceded for a man until he was forgiven: Tabarak alladhi biyadihil-mulk. The other two statements are correct.

statements: The archers' leaving their post turned the tide at Badr.
The first migration was to Abyssinia.
Backbiting is compared in the Qur'an to eating a dead brother's flesh.
medium.explain: At Uhud the archers left the hill against orders, and the Muslims were attacked from behind. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Interest (riba) is forbidden in the Qur'an.
Hamzah was martyred at Uhud.
Surah Al-Isra allows saying "uff" to parents.
medium.explain: Al-Isra commands goodness to parents and forbids even saying "uff". The other two statements are correct.

statements: Yahya was the son of Imran.
Abu Hurayrah narrated more hadith than any other companion.
Ayat al-Kursi is the greatest verse in the Qur'an.
medium.explain: Yahya was born to Zakariyya in his old age. The other two statements are correct.

statements: "Today I have perfected your religion" was revealed at Arafah.
The angels Munkar and Nakir question the dead in the grave.
Qarun drowned in the sea.
medium.explain: Allah caused the earth to swallow Qarun. Fir'awn drowned. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Dawud killed Jalut.
Luqman advised his son not to associate partners with Allah.
The Year of Sorrow saw the deaths of Abu Bakr and Umar.
medium.explain: Abu Talib and Khadijah died in the same year, before the Hijrah. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Allah does not burden a soul beyond what it can bear.
The Battle of Uhud is named in the Qur'an.
Shaytan flees from a house where Al-Baqarah is recited.
medium.explain: Surah At-Tawbah names Hunayn. Uhud is described but not named. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Ibrahim's father was named Imran in the Qur'an.
Tahajjud is prayed at night.
Zamzam appeared for Hajar and her son.
medium.explain: Surah Al-An'am names Ibrahim's father Azar. The other two statements are correct.

statements: The Prophet ﷺ said the upper hand is better than the lower hand.
The Prophet ﷺ said whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or stay silent.
The Hijrah took place in 610 CE.
medium.explain: The Hijrah was in 622 CE. Revelation began around 610 CE. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Ali slept in the Prophet's bed on the night of the Hijrah.
Musa will return before the end of time.
Zakariyya was the guardian of Maryam.
medium.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said the son of Maryam will descend as a just ruler. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Surah Al-Kahf has 110 ayahs.
Surah Al-Isra has 111 ayahs.
Surah Yusuf has 101 ayahs.
hard.explain: Surah Yusuf has 111 ayahs, the same count as Al-Isra. Al-Kahf has 110.

statements: Juz 30 is commonly called Juz Amma.
Juz 30 begins with Surah An-Naba.
Juz 30 contains 36 surahs.
hard.explain: Juz 30 runs from Surah An-Naba (78) to An-Nas (114), which is 37 surahs, not 36.

statements: The first revelation was the opening verses of Surah Al-Alaq.
Surah Al-Muddaththir came early, after the pause in revelation.
Surah Al-Fatihah was the first revelation.
hard.explain: The first revelation was Surah Al-Alaq, verses 1–5, at the cave of Hira. Al-Fatihah was revealed early in the Makkan period but was not the first.

statements: Surah Ar-Rahman repeats one verse 31 times.
That repeated verse asks which of the favours of your Lord you would deny.
Surah Ar-Rahman is part of juz 30.
hard.explain: Surah Ar-Rahman is surah 55 and falls in juz 27. Its refrain is repeated 31 times.

statements: The Prophet ﷺ passed away in 11 AH.
Abu Bakr's caliphate lasted roughly two years.
Umar's caliphate lasted roughly two years.
hard.explain: Umar's caliphate lasted about ten years, from 13 AH to 23 AH. Abu Bakr's was the short one, roughly two years.

statements: Surah At-Tawbah is the only surah that does not open with the Basmalah.
The Basmalah appears within Surah An-Naml.
Surah At-Tawbah is the shortest surah in the Qur'an.
hard.explain: Surah At-Tawbah has 129 ayahs and is one of the longer surahs. The shortest is Al-Kawthar, with three.

statements: Surah Al-Baqarah has 286 ayahs.
Surah Al-Imran has 200 ayahs.
Surah An-Nisa has 200 ayahs.
hard.explain: Surah An-Nisa has 176 ayahs. Al-Imran is the one with 200.

statements: Surah Al-An'am has 165 ayahs.
Surah Al-A'raf has 206 ayahs.
Surah Al-Ma'idah has 165 ayahs.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Ma'idah has 120 ayahs. It is Al-An'am that has 165.

statements: Surah Maryam is surah 19.
Surah Ta-Ha is surah 20.
Surah Al-Anbiya is surah 20.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Anbiya is surah 21. Surah 20 is Ta-Ha.

statements: Badr was fought in Ramadan of 2 AH.
Uhud was fought in 3 AH.
The conquest of Makkah took place in 6 AH.
hard.explain: The conquest of Makkah took place in Ramadan of 8 AH. The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was the event of 6 AH.

statements: Mu'tah was fought in 8 AH.
Tabuk took place in 9 AH.
Khaybar took place in 9 AH.
hard.explain: Khaybar took place in 7 AH, shortly after the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah.

statements: Abu Bakr's caliphate began in 11 AH.
Umar's caliphate began in 13 AH.
Uthman's caliphate began in 13 AH.
hard.explain: Uthman's caliphate began in 23 AH, after Umar's roughly ten-year rule.

statements: Surah Al-Kawthar has three ayahs.
Surah Al-Asr has three ayahs.
Surah An-Nasr has four ayahs.
hard.explain: Surah An-Nasr has three ayahs, like Al-Kawthar and Al-Asr.

statements: Juz 30 runs from An-Naba to An-Nas.
Juz 30 contains 37 surahs.
Juz 29 begins with Surah Al-Mulk, surah 68.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Mulk is surah 67, and juz 29 does begin with it. The surah number given is wrong; 68 is Al-Qalam.

statements: Surah Al-Fil refers to the Year of the Elephant.
Surah Quraysh follows Surah Al-Fil in the mushaf.
Surah Quraysh precedes Surah Al-Fil in the mushaf.
hard.explain: Al-Fil is surah 105 and Quraysh is surah 106, so Quraysh follows it.

statements: Surah Yusuf tells one continuous narrative.
Surah Yusuf has 111 ayahs.
Surah Yusuf is a Madinan surah.
hard.explain: Surah Yusuf is Makkan. It has 111 ayahs and is distinctive for telling a single sustained narrative.

statements: Al-Bukhari died in 870 CE.
Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj died in 875 CE.
Abu Dawud compiled one of the two Sahih collections.
hard.explain: The two Sahih collections are those of al-Bukhari and Muslim. Abu Dawud compiled a Sunan, one of the other four of the six books.

statements: Abu Hanifah died in 767 CE.
Malik ibn Anas died in 795 CE.
Al-Shafi'i died before Abu Hanifah.
hard.explain: Al-Shafi'i died in 820 CE, over fifty years after Abu Hanifah. The usual order is Abu Hanifah, Malik, al-Shafi'i, then Ahmad ibn Hanbal.

statements: Surah Ar-Rahman's refrain appears 31 times.
Surah Al-Mursalat also has a repeated refrain.
Surah Ar-Rahman is a surah of juz 30.
hard.explain: Surah Ar-Rahman is surah 55 and falls in juz 27. Al-Mursalat does have its own repeated refrain.

statements: The Prophet ﷺ passed away in Rabi al-Awwal.
The Hijrah took place in the month of Rabi al-Awwal.
The Hijri calendar begins its year with Rabi al-Awwal.
hard.explain: The Hijri year begins with Muharram. The calendar counts from the year of the Hijrah, but its first month is Muharram, not the month of the migration itself.

statements: Surah Al-Isra is also known as Bani Isra'il.
Surah Al-Isra has 111 ayahs.
Surah Al-Isra is also known as Surah Al-Mi'raj.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Isra (17) is also called Bani Isra'il. 'Surah Al-Mi'raj' is not one of its recognised names.

statements: Surah Al-Kahf is surah 18.
Surah Maryam is surah 19.
Surah Ta-Ha is surah 19.
hard.explain: Ta-Ha is surah 20, immediately after Maryam.

statements: Surah Al-Hajj contains a sajdah.
Surah As-Sajdah contains a sajdah.
Surah Al-Baqarah contains a sajdah.
hard.explain: Despite its length, Surah Al-Baqarah contains no verse of prostration.

statements: Khaybar was in 7 AH.
Hudaybiyyah was in 6 AH.
Hunayn was in 7 AH.
hard.explain: Hunayn was fought in 8 AH, shortly after the conquest of Makkah.

statements: Surah An-Naba has 40 ayahs.
Surah An-Nazi'at has 46 ayahs.
Surah Abasa has 60 ayahs.
hard.explain: Surah Abasa has 42 ayahs.

statements: Al-Nasa'i died in 915 CE.
Al-Tirmidhi died in 892 CE.
Al-Nasa'i died before al-Tirmidhi.
hard.explain: Al-Nasa'i outlived al-Tirmidhi by more than twenty years; he was the last of the six compilers to die.

statements: Surah Al-Imran has 200 ayahs.
Surah Al-Ma'idah has 120 ayahs.
Surah Al-Anfal has 120 ayahs.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Anfal has 75 ayahs.

statements: The Battle of Siffin was fought during Ali's caliphate.
The Battle of the Camel was fought during Ali's caliphate.
The Battle of Siffin was fought during Uthman's caliphate.
hard.explain: Both Siffin and the Battle of the Camel took place during the caliphate of Ali, in the period of civil conflict known as the first fitnah.

statements: Surah Al-Fath was revealed in connection with Hudaybiyyah.
Surah Al-Anfal relates largely to Badr.
Surah Al-Hashr relates largely to Badr.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Hashr concerns the exile of Banu al-Nadir, not Badr.

statements: Surah Yunus is surah 10.
Surah Hud is surah 11.
Surah Ibrahim is surah 13.
hard.explain: Surah Ibrahim is surah 14. Surah 13 is Ar-Ra'd.

statements: Malik ibn Anas compiled the Muwatta.
Ahmad ibn Hanbal compiled a Musnad.
Al-Shafi'i compiled the Muwatta.
hard.explain: The Muwatta is Malik's. Al-Shafi'i, who studied under Malik, is known for al-Risalah and al-Umm.

statements: The Hijri calendar was formally instituted during Umar's caliphate.
Its first year corresponds to 622 CE.
It was formally instituted during Abu Bakr's caliphate.
hard.explain: The calendar was formally established under Umar, who set its starting point at the year of the Hijrah.

statements: Surah Al-Waqi'ah is surah 56.
Surah Al-Hadid is surah 57.
Surah Ar-Rahman is surah 56.
hard.explain: Surah Ar-Rahman is surah 55, immediately before Al-Waqi'ah.

statements: Zayd ibn Thabit led the compilation under Abu Bakr.
He was also central to the standardisation under Uthman.
He was a Muhajir from Makkah.
hard.explain: Zayd ibn Thabit was from Madinah and so was among the Ansar, not the Muhajirun.

statements: Surah Al-Mulk has 30 ayahs.
Surah Nuh has 28 ayahs.
Surah Al-Jinn has 18 ayahs.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Jinn has 28 ayahs. Surah Al-Jinn and Surah Nuh both have 28.

statements: The Prophet ﷺ was born in the Year of the Elephant by the traditional account.
He was about forty at the first revelation.
He was about thirty at the first revelation.
hard.explain: The traditional account places the first revelation at about the age of forty.

statements: Surah Al-Ankabut is surah 29.
Surah Ar-Rum is surah 30.
Surah As-Sajdah is surah 31.
hard.explain: As-Sajdah is surah 32. Surah 31 is Luqman.

statements: Abu Hanifah is associated with Kufa.
Malik ibn Anas is associated with Madinah.
Ahmad ibn Hanbal is associated with Madinah.
hard.explain: Ahmad ibn Hanbal is associated with Baghdad. Malik is the one associated with Madinah.

statements: Surah Al-Qadr describes a night better than a thousand months.
Surah Al-Qadr has five ayahs.
Surah Al-Qadr is a Madinan surah.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Qadr (97) is generally classified as Makkan, though a minority view holds otherwise.

statements: Tabuk took place in 9 AH.
The Farewell Pilgrimage took place in 10 AH.
The Farewell Pilgrimage took place in 9 AH.
hard.explain: The Farewell Pilgrimage was in 10 AH, the year before the Prophet's passing in 11 AH.

statements: Surah Al-Fil has five ayahs.
Surah Quraysh has four ayahs.
Surah Al-Ma'un has four ayahs.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Ma'un has seven ayahs.

statements: Surah Al-Ahzab is surah 33.
It contains the verse naming the Prophet ﷺ the seal of the prophets.
It is a Makkan surah.
hard.explain: Al-Ahzab is Madinan; it relates to the Confederates who besieged Madinah at Khandaq.

statements: Surah Al-Anfal relates largely to Badr.
Surah At-Tawbah follows it in the mushaf.
Surah Al-Anfal has 129 ayahs.
hard.explain: Al-Anfal has 75 ayahs. It is At-Tawbah that has 129.

statements: Surah Qaf is surah 50.
Surah Sad is surah 38.
Surah Nun is the common name of surah 67.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Qalam, which opens with the letter Nun, is surah 68. Surah 67 is Al-Mulk.

statements: Al-Sab' al-Tiwal begins with Al-Baqarah.
Its seventh member is disputed.
It consists of nine surahs.
hard.explain: The name means 'the seven long ones'. The dispute concerns which surah occupies the seventh place.

statements: Ibn Khaldun wrote the Muqaddimah.
He died in 1406 CE.
He wrote Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Azim.
hard.explain: That tafsir is Ibn Kathir's. Ibn Khaldun is known for the Muqaddimah and his universal history.

statements: Surah Al-Mumtahanah is surah 60.
Surah As-Saff is surah 61.
Surah Al-Hashr is surah 61.
hard.explain: Al-Hashr is surah 59. As-Saff is 61.

statements: Zayd ibn Thabit was of the Ansar.
He led the compilation under Abu Bakr.
He was among the Muhajirun.
hard.explain: He was from Madinah, and so of the Ansar rather than the emigrants from Makkah.

statements: The Saqifah gathering followed the Prophet's passing.
It concluded with allegiance to Abu Bakr.
It concluded with allegiance to Umar.
hard.explain: Abu Bakr was given the pledge at the Saqifah. Umar succeeded him two years later.

statements: Surah Muhammad is surah 47.
It is also called Surah al-Qital.
It is the only surah named after a prophet.
hard.explain: Six surahs are named after prophets. Surah Muhammad is the only one named after the Prophet ﷺ himself.

statements: Al-Mufassal is the final portion of the mushaf.
Scholars differ over where it begins.
Al-Mufassal is the opening portion of the mushaf.
hard.explain: Al-Mufassal is the concluding section of shorter surahs. The opening section is al-Sab' al-Tiwal.

statements: Muhkam and mutashabih are mentioned in Surah Al-Imran.
Muhkam verses are clear in meaning.
Mutashabih verses are the clear ones.
hard.explain: It is the reverse: muhkam are the clear verses, mutashabih those admitting more than one reading.

statements: Surah Al-Hujurat is surah 49.
Surah Qaf is surah 50.
Surah Adh-Dhariyat is surah 52.
hard.explain: Adh-Dhariyat is surah 51. Surah 52 is At-Tur.

statements: Abu Sufyan commanded at Uhud.
He accepted Islam at the conquest of Makkah.
He was killed at Badr.
hard.explain: Abu Jahl was killed at Badr. Abu Sufyan lived on and accepted Islam in 8 AH.

statements: Surah Ar-Ra'd is surah 13.
Surah Ibrahim is surah 14.
Surah Al-Hijr is surah 16.
hard.explain: Al-Hijr is surah 15. Surah 16 is An-Nahl.

statements: The first fitnah included Siffin.
It fell within Ali's caliphate.
It fell within Uthman's caliphate.
hard.explain: The first fitnah followed Uthman's killing and unfolded during Ali's caliphate.

statements: Surah Al-Fath has 29 ayahs.
It refers to Hudaybiyyah as a clear victory.
It has 129 ayahs.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Fath has 29 ayahs. At-Tawbah is the surah with 129.

Kalalah is someone who leaves neither parent nor child.
The Prophet ﷺ forbade shaving the head in Hajj.
hard.explain: He prayed for those who shave, then included those who trim. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Abu Dharr's name was Jundub ibn Junadah.
A mawquf report is raised to the Prophet ﷺ.
The Prophet ﷺ performed four umrahs.
hard.explain: Mawquf stops at a companion. A report raised to the Prophet ﷺ is marfu'. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Al-Samiri made the golden calf.
Abdullah ibn Salam was a Jewish scholar of Madinah before Islam.
Malik studied under al-Shafi'i.
hard.explain: Al-Shafi'i, the younger, studied the Muwatta' under Malik in Madinah. The other two statements are correct.

statements: The Prophet's she-camel al-Qaswa' knelt at Badr and refused to fight.
Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz ruled for about two and a half years.
Ahmad, as a name of the Prophet ﷺ, appears in Surah As-Saff.
hard.explain: Al-Qaswa' knelt at Hudaybiyyah. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Salman al-Farisi came from Persia.
Hafsah was the daughter of Abu Bakr.
Al-Tabari wrote both a tafsir and a history.
hard.explain: Hafsah was Umar's daughter. Aishah was Abu Bakr's. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Umar's caliphate lasted about one year.
Ayat al-Dayn is the longest verse in the Qur'an.
A mursal hadith omits the companion from the chain.
hard.explain: Umar ruled from 13 to 23 AH. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Seven angels enter al-Bayt al-Ma'mur every year.
Talut tested his army by forbidding them to drink from a river.
The Qur'an gives the husband four months in the case of ila'.
hard.explain: The Prophet ﷺ was told seventy thousand angels pray in it daily. The other two statements are correct.

statements: The prayers were first prescribed as three and increased to five.
Musa is the prophet named most often in the Qur'an.
The expiation for zihar includes fasting two consecutive months.
hard.explain: On Musa's advice the Prophet ﷺ asked for a reduction until they became five. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Thumamah ibn Uthal was tied to a pillar of the mosque before accepting Islam.
Zayd is named in Surah Al-Ahzab.
Days of Tashriq are the first three days of Shawwal.
hard.explain: They are the three days after the Day of Sacrifice. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Surah Al-Kahf contains a basmalah in the middle of the surah.
The white days are the 13th, 14th and 15th of the lunar month.
Ibn Hajar wrote Fath al-Bari on Sahih al-Bukhari.
hard.explain: Sulayman's letter in Surah An-Naml begins with the basmalah. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Aishah gave her day to Sawdah.
The believer of Fir'awn's family hid his faith.
Abu Hanifah died in 150 AH.
hard.explain: Sawdah gave her turn to Aishah. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Dhul-Qarnayn stayed in one city all his life.
Hudhayfah urged Uthman to unify the copies of the Qur'an.
Sa'd ibn Mu'adh judged the case of Banu Qurayzah.
hard.explain: Al-Kahf describes his journeys west and east. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Idris is named twenty times in the Qur'an.
The Battle of Ain Jalut was fought against the Mongols.
The siege of Ta'if came after the Battle of Hunayn.
hard.explain: Idris is named in Maryam and Al-Anbiya. The other two statements are correct.

statements: The Dome of the Rock was built under Harun al-Rashid.
Umar was stabbed while leading the prayer in the mosque.
Umar appointed six men to choose the next caliph.
hard.explain: Abd al-Malik built it, completed in 72 AH. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Al-Khidr demanded payment for rebuilding a wall.
Zaynab bint Jahsh was previously married to Zayd ibn Harithah.
Safiyyah's dowry was her freedom.
hard.explain: Musa suggested payment, but al-Khidr repaired it freely for two orphans. The other two statements are correct.

statements: The Prophet's ring was engraved "Muhammad Messenger of Allah".
Juwayriyah was the daughter of the chief of Quraysh.
Expiation for a broken oath can be feeding ten poor people.
hard.explain: She was the daughter of the chief of Banu al-Mustaliq. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Abu Ayyub al-Ansari is buried near Constantinople.
Umar entered al-Sham during the plague to lead the prayer there.
Al-Shafi'i died in Egypt.
hard.explain: On hearing the Prophet's instruction he returned. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Uthman was martyred at Siffin.
Al-Tirmidhi often graded hadith as hasan in his Jami'.
Zaynab bint Jahsh was previously married to Zayd ibn Harithah.
hard.explain: Uthman was killed by rebels in his house in 35 AH. The other two statements are correct.

statements: The miqat for the people of al-Sham is al-Juhfah.
Sa'd ibn Mu'adh judged the case of Banu Qurayzah.
Seven hundred reciters were killed at Bi'r Ma'unah.
hard.explain: The Prophet ﷺ sent seventy reciters, who were betrayed and killed. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Banu Qaynuqa' were the first Jewish tribe expelled from Madinah.
A fifth of the spoils is set aside in Surah Al-Anfal.
Surah Al-Hashr was revealed about Abu Lahab.
hard.explain: Ibn Abbas called Al-Hashr the surah of Banu al-Nadir. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Imam al-Bukhari was a student of Imam Muslim.
The Battle of Ain Jalut was fought against the Mongols.
Abdullah ibn Salam was a Jewish scholar of Madinah before Islam.
hard.explain: Muslim studied under al-Bukhari, who was older. The other two statements are correct.

statements: The Qur'an was gathered under Abu Bakr after many reciters died at Badr.
A hadith qudsi is narrated by the Prophet ﷺ from Allah.
In li'an each spouse swears four times and then a fifth oath.
hard.explain: Umar urged Abu Bakr after many reciters were killed at Yamamah. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Days of Tashriq are the first three days of Shawwal.
The Battle of the Camel was fought near Basra.
Idris is named twice in the Qur'an.
hard.explain: They are the three days after the Day of Sacrifice. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Hafs narrated the recitation of 'Asim.
Ahmad, as a name of the Prophet ﷺ, appears in Surah As-Saff.
Zayd is named in Surah Al-Baqarah.
hard.explain: Al-Ahzab 37 names Zayd. The other two statements are correct.

statements: The Hijri calendar was adopted under Umar.
The Prophet ﷺ met Ibrahim in the first heaven on the Mi'raj.
The sheets of the Qur'an were kept with Hafsah before Uthman's copies.
hard.explain: He met Adam in the first heaven and Ibrahim in the seventh. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Al-Shafi'i died in Yemen.
Umar's caliphate lasted about ten years.
Baghdad was founded by the Abbasid caliph al-Mansur.
hard.explain: Al-Shafi'i spent his last years in Egypt and died there in 204 AH. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Ibn Hajar wrote Fath al-Bari on Sahih Muslim.
Safiyyah's dowry was her freedom.
Malik ibn Anas compiled al-Muwatta'.
hard.explain: Fath al-Bari explains Sahih al-Bukhari. Al-Nawawi's commentary is on Sahih Muslim. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Ahmad ibn Hanbal studied under al-Shafi'i.
The plague of Amwas struck Makkah in Abu Bakr's time.
A mursal hadith omits the companion from the chain.
hard.explain: It struck al-Sham around 18 AH, and Abu Ubaydah died in it. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Al-Tabari wrote both a tafsir and a history.
Salman al-Farisi came from Persia.
Khalid ibn al-Walid urged Uthman to unify the copies of the Qur'an.
hard.explain: Hudhayfah, alarmed by differences in recitation, came to Uthman. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Granada was the last Muslim kingdom in al-Andalus.
Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz ruled for about forty years.
Uthman was martyred in his house in Madinah.
hard.explain: He ruled from 99 to 101 AH. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Isa is called Kalimullah because Allah spoke to him on Mount Sinai.
The Mongols sacked Baghdad in 656 AH.
Qarn al-Manazil is the miqat for the people of Najd.
hard.explain: Allah spoke to Musa directly. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Umar appointed his son as the next caliph.
Asma bint Abi Bakr is called the one with two waistbands.
Imam al-Bukhari died in 256 AH.
hard.explain: Umar named six of the companions as a council. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Seventy prophets are named in the Qur'an.
Umar was stabbed while leading the prayer in the mosque.
The incident of the Ifk happened on the return from Banu al-Mustaliq.
hard.explain: Twenty-five prophets and messengers are named. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Surah Al-Mujadilah mentions the name of Allah in every verse.
Abu Bakr's caliphate lasted about two years.
The white days are the 1st, 2nd and 3rd of the lunar month.
hard.explain: The Prophet ﷺ advised fasting the 13th, 14th and 15th. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas commanded the Muslims at Qadisiyyah.
Abu Musa al-Ash'ari came from Persia.
The believer of Fir'awn's family hid his faith.
hard.explain: He was of the Ash'ari tribe of Yemen. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Al-Nawawi compiled Riyad as-Salihin.
The Battle of Yamamah was fought against Musaylimah.
Ibn Taymiyyah was a student of Ibn Kathir.
hard.explain: Ibn Kathir (d. 774 AH) studied under Ibn Taymiyyah (d. 728 AH). The other two statements are correct.

statements: Al-Tirmidhi often graded hadith as hasan in his Jami'.
Ammar ibn Yasir was killed at Badr.
The prayers were first prescribed as fifty and reduced to five.
hard.explain: Ammar was killed at Siffin in 37 AH. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Expiation for a broken oath is feeding one hundred poor people.
The Prophet ﷺ prayed for those who shave their heads three times in Hajj.
Sawdah gave her day to Aishah.
hard.explain: Al-Ma'idah 89 names feeding ten needy people. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Isa spoke as a baby in the cradle.
Ka'b ibn Malik led the army to Tabuk.
Juwayriyah's people were freed after her marriage to the Prophet ﷺ.
hard.explain: Ka'b told the story of how he stayed behind and was forgiven. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Al-Shafi'i studied under Malik.
Al-Qaswa' was the mount of the Night Journey.
Dhul-Qarnayn travelled to where the sun sets and where it rises.
hard.explain: The Prophet ﷺ rode al-Buraq on the Isra. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Al-Khidr rebuilt a falling wall without asking for payment.
Abdullah ibn Ubayy led the archers at Uhud.
Umar turned back from al-Sham because of the plague.
hard.explain: He turned back with about a third of the army. The archers were led by Abdullah ibn Jubayr. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Ahmad ibn Hanbal was persecuted in the Mihnah over the createdness of the Qur'an.
The Qur'an gives the husband four years in the case of ila'.
Umar set Dhat 'Irq as the miqat for Iraq.
hard.explain: Al-Baqarah 226: a wait of four months. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Ayat al-Kursi is the longest verse in the Qur'an.
Musa is the prophet named most often in the Qur'an.
The siege of Ta'if came after the Battle of Hunayn.
hard.explain: The verse of debt, Al-Baqarah 282, is the longest. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Seventy thousand angels enter al-Bayt al-Ma'mur every day.
The Prophet ﷺ made qunut against the killers of the reciters for a month.
Ibn Ishaq edited the Sirah of Ibn Hisham.
hard.explain: Ibn Ishaq wrote the earlier biography. Ibn Hisham edited it. The other two statements are correct.

statements: A mawquf report stops at a companion.
The six books of hadith include Sunan Ibn Majah.
The Qur'an calls Nuh "Khalil", the intimate friend of Allah.
hard.explain: Allah took Ibrahim as a close friend. The other two statements are correct.

statements: The People of the Ditch are mentioned in Surah Al-Buruj.
The Prophet ﷺ performed forty umrahs.
Talut tested his army by forbidding them to drink from a river.
hard.explain: Anas said four umrahs. The other two statements are correct.

statements: The Umayyad capital was Damascus.
Abu Ayyub al-Ansari is buried in Yemen.
The People of the Sabbath were turned into apes.
hard.explain: He died on the expedition to Constantinople and was buried near its walls. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Abu Dharr's name was Abd al-Rahman ibn Sakhr.
The Prophet's she-camel al-Qaswa' knelt at Hudaybiyyah.
Salah al-Din retook Jerusalem after the Battle of Hattin.
hard.explain: Abu Dharr was Jundub ibn Junadah. Abd al-Rahman ibn Sakhr is a name given for Abu Hurayrah. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Abu Hanifah died in 250 AH.
The Dome of the Rock was built under Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan.
The expiation for zihar includes fasting two consecutive months.
hard.explain: Abu Hanifah died in 150 AH, the year al-Shafi'i was born. The other two statements are correct.

statements: The name Muhammad appears forty times in the Qur'an.
Hafsah was the daughter of Umar.
A bequest is limited to a third of the estate.
hard.explain: It appears in Ali 'Imran, Al-Ahzab, Muhammad and Al-Fath. The other two statements are correct.

statements: The Throne shook at the death of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh.
Surah An-Naml contains a basmalah in the middle of the surah.
The Prophet's ring was engraved with his date of birth.
hard.explain: He had a silver ring engraved Muhammad Rasul Allah. The other two statements are correct.

events.text: The first revelation at the cave of Hira

easy.explain: The first revelation came around 610 CE. The migration to Madinah followed about twelve years later, in 622 CE.

events.text: The birth of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ

easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ was born around 570 CE. Makkah was conquered peacefully in 8 AH, 630 CE, around sixty years later.
The Hijrah was in 622 CE and the Farewell Pilgrimage in 10 AH, 632 CE, shortly before the Prophet ﷺ passed away.

events.text: The passing of the Prophet ﷺ

easy.explain: Badr was fought in 2 AH, 624 CE. The Prophet ﷺ passed away in 11 AH, 632 CE.
The Year of the Elephant is traditionally placed around the year of the Prophet's birth, about forty years before the first revelation.

events.text: The first revelation at the cave of Hira

easy.explain: Revelation began around 610 CE. Makkah was entered peacefully twenty years later, in 8 AH.
Masjid Quba was built on arrival in Madinah at the very start of the Madinan period. The Farewell Pilgrimage came nine years later, shortly before the Prophet's passing.

events.text: The Prophet ﷺ receives his first revelation
The Prophet ﷺ passes away in Madinah

easy.explain: Around twenty-two years separate the first revelation from the Prophet's passing in Madinah.

events.text: The caliphate of Uthman ibn Affan begins

easy.explain: Badr was fought in the second year after the Hijrah; Uthman became caliph twenty-one years later.
A group of Muslims first sought refuge in Abyssinia around 615 CE, some seven years before the migration to Madinah.

events.text: The birth of the Prophet ﷺ

easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ was around fifty-two at the time of the Hijrah.

events.text: The caliphate of Abu Bakr begins

easy.explain: Hudaybiyyah came five years before the Prophet's passing and the accession of Abu Bakr.
The Year of the Elephant is traditionally placed around the Prophet's birth, some fifty-four years before Badr.
Around seventeen years passed between the start of public preaching in Makkah and the city's peaceful conquest.

events.text: The change of qiblah to the Ka'bah

easy.explain: The qiblah was changed early in the Madinan period; Tabuk was the last major expedition, seven years later.
The Prophet ﷺ married Khadijah around fifteen years before the first revelation came to him at the cave of Hira.
The Prophet ﷺ was about thirty-five when he settled the Quraysh dispute over placing the Black Stone, some seventeen years before the Hijrah.
The night journey took place in the final Makkan years, about a decade before Makkah was entered peacefully.
Seven years separate Uhud from the Farewell Pilgrimage, which came shortly before the Prophet's passing.
Thirty-four years separate the migration from the beginning of Ali's caliphate.
The siege of Madinah at Khandaq came four years before the expedition to Tabuk, the last the Prophet ﷺ led in person.

events.text: The passing of the Prophet ﷺ

easy.explain: Abu Bakr and Umar led in the twelve years between the Prophet's passing and Uthman's accession.
About eighteen years separate the beginning of revelation from the truce at Hudaybiyyah.

events.text: The boycott of Banu Hashim begins

easy.explain: The Makkan boycott preceded the Hijrah; Badr was fought two years after the migration.
The Prophet ﷺ was around forty-three when the call became public, three years after the first revelation.

events.text: The caliphate of Abu Bakr begins

easy.explain: Three years separate the conquest of Makkah from the Prophet's passing and Abu Bakr's accession.
Five years separate Badr from Khaybar, which followed the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah.

events.text: The caliphate of Hasan ibn Ali

easy.explain: Twenty-seven years and three caliphates separate the start of Umar's rule from Hasan's brief caliphate.
Al-Bukhari belongs to the third Islamic century; Ibn Kathir, the mufassir and historian, to the eighth.
Abu Hanifah is the earliest of the four school founders; al-Ghazali lived more than three centuries later.

events.text: The change of qiblah to the Ka'bah

easy.explain: The qiblah changed early in the Madinan period, eight years before the Farewell Sermon.
The pledge that enabled the Hijrah came shortly before the migration; Uhud followed three years later.
The flight to Abyssinia belongs to the years of persecution in Makkah; Tabuk came fifteen years later.
The Year of Sorrow, with the loss of Khadijah and Abu Talib, came about eleven years before tribes began arriving in Madinah in numbers.
Masjid Quba was built on arrival in Madinah; Hunayn was fought seven years later, just after the conquest of Makkah.

events.text: The compilation of the Qur'an under Abu Bakr
The standardisation of copies under Uthman

easy.explain: The written collection was gathered under Abu Bakr; standard copies were produced and distributed under Uthman more than a decade later.
Umar accepted Islam during the Makkan years of persecution, about eighteen years before becoming caliph.

events.text: The passing of the Prophet ﷺ

easy.explain: Mu'tah was fought three years before the Prophet's passing, earlier in the same year as the conquest of Makkah.
Khadijah died about five years before Badr, in the Year of Sorrow.
Umar accepted Islam during the Makkan persecution, about fourteen years before Makkah was entered.
Six years separate Uhud from Tabuk, the last expedition the Prophet ﷺ led in person.
About twenty-six years separate the first revelation from the decisive battle in Syria under Umar.
Four years separate the truce at Hudaybiyyah from the Farewell Pilgrimage.

events.text: The caliphate of Abu Bakr begins

easy.explain: Twenty-four years and two caliphates separate the first and fourth of the Rashidun.
Three years separate the siege of Madinah from Hunayn, fought just after the conquest of Makkah.
About eleven years separate the start of the public call from the first major battle.

events.text: The passing of the Prophet ﷺ

easy.explain: Al-Bukhari compiled his collection more than two centuries after the Prophet's passing.
More than five centuries separate the founder of the Maliki school from Ibn Taymiyyah.

events.text: The standardisation of the Qur'an under Uthman

easy.explain: The losses at Yamamah prompted the first written compilation; the standardisation of copies came more than a decade later.

events.text: The martyrdom of Husayn at Karbala

easy.explain: Fifty-three years separate Mu'tah, in the Prophet's lifetime, from Karbala.
Eighteen years and two caliphates separate Uthman's accession from the beginning of Umayyad rule.

events.text: The Prophet ﷺ is orphaned of his mother Aminah

easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ lost his mother at about six years of age, some thirty-four years before revelation began.

events.text: Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib accepts Islam

easy.explain: Hamza accepted Islam during the Makkan years and was killed at Uhud, about nine years later.

events.text: Bilal ibn Rabah is persecuted in Makkah
Bilal gives the adhan at the conquest of Makkah

easy.explain: Bilal was tortured for his faith in Makkah and later called the adhan from atop the Ka'bah when the city was taken.

events.text: The Muslims are commanded to face Jerusalem in prayer
The qiblah is changed to the Ka'bah

easy.explain: Jerusalem was the first qiblah; the direction was changed to the Ka'bah in the second year after the Hijrah.

events.text: Ja'far ibn Abi Talib leads the migrants in Abyssinia

easy.explain: Ja'far spoke for the Muslims before the Negus in Abyssinia and was killed years later at Mu'tah.

events.text: Salman al-Farisi suggests digging a trench

easy.explain: Salman's suggestion shaped the defence of Madinah at Khandaq, three years before Makkah was entered.

events.text: Mus'ab ibn Umayr is sent to teach in Yathrib

easy.explain: Mus'ab was sent to Yathrib after the first Pledge of Aqabah and was killed at Uhud a few years later.
Abu Bakr was among the first to believe and became the first caliph some twenty-two years later.

events.text: Khalid ibn al-Walid fights against the Muslims at Uhud
Khalid commands Muslim forces at Yarmuk

easy.explain: Khalid fought against the Muslims at Uhud, accepted Islam before the conquest of Makkah, and later commanded at Yarmuk.

easy.explain: After his mother's death the Prophet ﷺ was cared for by his grandfather, and on his death about two years later by his uncle Abu Talib.
